verdicts.why: Plain farming verb for raising crops; it names the activity and takes no side on it.
Coming to have a beard or more height is a bare physical change; nothing about the speaker's attitude rides on the word.
Coming into existence or taking shape is described flatly; no approval or dismissal attaches.
Maturing emotionally is a positive-direction meaning, not an attitude beyond it; the word reports development without editorialising.
Causing something to develop is a neutral causative; no judgement of the thing grown or the grower.
Becoming attached as if by growth (a graft, a fused bone) is descriptive and carries no stance.
A ballpark is a place where games are played; the word names the facility and judges nothing.
A gear position is a mechanical label with no attitude in it.
Someone under consideration for a place or prize is named as a candidate; the potential is the meaning, not a verdict on the person.
A prognosis is a medical prediction; the disease is the bad referent, the word itself is neutral.
Reaching a conclusion after deliberation is the plain verb for that mental act; no approval or contempt in it.
Concluding a treaty or bargain is formal register but not an attitude; it describes closing an agreement.
Being able to hold a quantity is pure capacity; nothing is judged.
Holding back a danger or enemy treats the object as a threat by meaning, not by added attitude; the verb reports the check without sneering or praising.
Divisibility is arithmetic; there is no stance to warn a learner about.
A hint of something is a small amount; the word measures rather than judges.
An indication of a possible opportunity (a tip, a lead) names the information neutrally, with no attitude toward giver or receiver.
Causing someone to decide, or a matter being decided, reports settlement without commending or belittling it.
Bringing forth or yielding a result, a book, or a son-in-law is described flatly; the verb itself takes no side.
Bringing something onto the market is a commercial act named plainly; no approval or dismissal is built in.
Raising crops is farming vocabulary with no attitude in it.
Undergoing a change of physical features is a neutral description of change.
Identifying a species in botany or biology is technical and takes no stance on what is described.
Placing or fixing something firmly on a base is a mechanical description with no judgement.
Providing seats or seating guests names a plain action; the word carries no attitude toward those seated.
Formally placing someone in office is ceremonial register, not an attitude; the verb neither praises nor mocks the appointment.
Putting a seat on a chair is an act of repair or manufacture; nothing is judged.
The legal seizure of property is an unpleasant referent named in a technical term; the word itself does not side with creditor or debtor.
Putting someone in a dangerous or disadvantageous position describes the placement; the danger is the referent, and the verb adds no contempt or approval of its own.
Revealing to view by removing a cover is a physical description with no stance on what is uncovered.
